title: Relative pseudo-coherence under composition with a pseudo-coherent base
statement: Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\to S$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $X\to S$, $Y\to S$ and $f$ locally of finite type [def-pc-morphism-conventions]. Suppose that $\mathcal O_Y[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $S$ [def-sfb-relative-pseudo-coherent-complex]. For every integer $m$ and every $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-derived-category], $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$ if and only if $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$. There is no quasi-coherence hypothesis on $E$ and no Noetherian hypothesis on the schemes.

proof.text: Choose an affine cover of $S$ by $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$; over each $W$ choose affine opens $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ covering its inverse image in $Y$, and over each $V$ choose affine opens $U=\operatorname{Spec}B$ covering $f^{-1}V$. Such covers exist by the locally-finite-type definition. The all-affine-charts lemma supplies closed embeddings $k:V\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_W$ and $i:U\hookrightarrow T=\mathbf A^r_V$. Put $Q=\mathbf A^{n+r}_W$, and let $j:T\hookrightarrow Q$ be obtained from $k$ by adjoining the $r$ coordinates; write $l=ji$. Explicitly, from $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ one gets $R[x_1,\ldots,x_n,t_1,\ldots,t_r]\twoheadrightarrow A[t_1,\ldots,t_r]\twoheadrightarrow B$. These surjections show directly that $j$ and $l$ are closed immersions, and $j$ is the base change of $k$ by $\mathbf A^r_W\to W$. The integers $n,r\geq0$ are independent of the approximation degree $m$.

For every integer $a$, apply the all-affine-charts criterion to $\mathcal O_Y[0]$ and the pair $(V,W)$: $Rk_*(\mathcal O_V[0])$ is $a$-pseudo-coherent. The relative definition, with the single charts $V,W,k$, implies that $\mathcal O_V[0]$ is pseudo-coherent relative to $W$. The polynomial projection $\mathbf A^r_W\to W$ is flat by the polynomial-projection lemma. Apply flat relative base change to obtain pseudo-coherence of $\mathcal O_T[0]$ relative to $\mathbf A^r_W$. Indeed its derived pullback is $\mathcal O_T[0]$: tensor the free rank-one structure module with the new structure ring in the derived-pullback formula. Now apply the all-affine-charts criterion to the embedding $j:T\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_{\mathbf A^r_W}=Q$, for every $a$. Thus $Rj_*(\mathcal O_T[0])$ is absolutely pseudo-coherent on $Q$ (all finite stages).

Closed-immersion direct image is exact on underlying abelian sheaves by the cited exactness lemma. For module sheaves the same assertion follows by retaining the scalar actions on kernels and cokernels. Consequently $Ri_*,Rj_*,Rl_*$ are computed on every representing complex by termwise $i_*,j_*,l_*$. For an open $H\subset Q$ and each term $F$, $(j_*i_*F)(H)=F(i^{-1}j^{-1}H)=(l_*F)(H)$, with the same scalar action. Hence, for $K=Ri_*(E|_U)$, there is an identification $Rj_*K\cong Rl_*(E|_U)$. This also justifies the ordinary structure-module pushforwards used in step 2. In particular $Rj_*(\mathcal O_T[0])=(j_*\mathcal O_T)[0]$, so step 2 gives pseudo-coherence of the ordinary pushed-forward structure module.

Fix the integer $m$ in the statement. Apply the closed-pushforward pseudo-coherence lemma to $j:T\hookrightarrow Q$ and $K=Ri_*(E|_U)\in D(\mathcal O_T)$. Steps 2 and 3 supply its sole extra hypothesis, the pseudo-coherence of $(j_*\mathcal O_T)[0]$. Using step 3, it gives $Ri_*(E|_U)$ absolutely $m$-pseudo-coherent if and only if $Rl_*(E|_U)$ absolutely $m$-pseudo-coherent. It imposes no quasi-coherence or boundedness hypothesis on $E|_U$.

If $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $Y$, the all-affine-charts criterion makes $Ri_*(E|_U)$ absolutely $m$-pseudo-coherent for every chosen $(U,V,i)$. Step 4 gives the same property for $Rl_*(E|_U)$. For each $W$, the chosen $U$ cover the inverse image of $W$ in $X$ and $l:U\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^{n+r}_W$ is a closed immersion over $W$; these are exactly the witnesses in the relative definition for $E$ over $S$. Conversely, if $E$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent relative to $S$, the all-affine-charts criterion applied to $(U,W,l)$ gives the property for $Rl_*(E|_U)$, and step 4 gives it for $Ri_*(E|_U)$. The chosen $V$ cover $Y$, and for each $V$ the chosen $U$ cover $f^{-1}V$, so the relative definition with embeddings $i$ proves the assertion over $Y$. This proves both directions for every integer $m$.
